workOrders.title: BrandTheme.chrome is single-valued, so a two-mode tenant cannot author both
workOrders.evidence: Every control is readable against its own background, in every mode its tenant declares a ground for. MEASURED, before -> after (Rec.709 luminance delta between an element computed background and its own computed text): evnto native select 23.6 -> 213.4; evnto primary badge 23.6 -> 212+. Both were white on white. THE ROOT CAUSE WAS PARTLY MINE. WO-TOK-08 wired --ds-color-bg-input from chrome.controls.input.bg, which is right -- but it put the emission inside the CHROME emitter, and the generator applies chrome into the dark block too (darkChromeVars, WO-TOK-05). So a light-authored chrome leaked a white control surface into every tenant dark mode. Invisible until WO-ENG-17 gave evnto the modern engine it declares and WO-ENG-18 made me look. The semantic surface now lives in brandThemeToCssVariables (base block, from the same tenant channel) and NOT in the chrome emitter. The dark block deliberately does not emit it: a literal there would overwrite a dynamic dark tenant own declared surface -- torture-dark asks for #1A0014 and would have painted slate. I tried exactly that and the torture probe caught it. The design system cannot tell which mode a single-valued chrome was authored for, and guessing is worse than the bug; that ambiguity is what this WO names and what a future chrome-per-mode contract must resolve. NINTH INSTANCE OF THE ARCHETYPE: generator:299 and :330 already call getReadableForegroundColor for --ds-color-primary-foreground, while :549 hardcoded --ds-color-text-on-primary: #ffffff three lines away. It now derives. A HYPOTHESIS THE CODE REFUTED: I assumed the badge read --ds-color-text-on-primary. It reads --ds-color-primary-foreground. Reading its inline style settled it in one command; the hardcode I fixed was real and next door, but it was not this badge channel. evnto dark residue now declares both, plus its own dark control surface; bithire dark residue no longer declares a white one. NEW PIXEL GATE: packages/showroom/e2e/visual/contrast.spec.ts, 16 tests (4 tenants x 4 controls), reading COMPUTED background against COMPUTED text in the browser. Nothing is inferred from a token name. Threshold 60 is arithmetic: the two defects measured 23.6, the healthy controls on the same page measure 213.4 / 215.4 / 220.8, so it sits an order of magnitude above the defect and far below every healthy reading. A missing element is a HARD failure, never a passing skip.
